why: Expression cycle 4 (docs/v3/cycles/expression-4.md) lost 66 of 110 round-0 points to `skill`, 11 of its 16 P2s. The look step v3-expr-3-skill added ran: every builder opened its own frames, and two of six shot a keyboard frame without being asked. What they missed is the text's content, not the step. Four defects are in the shipped text itself: (a) `references/linked-parts.md` passes `focus` to `CartesianChart`, which renders `focus.live` (`src/charts/parts/cartesian.tsx:472`), and then renders `{focus.live}` again, so the two builders who followed it announce every step twice (c15, n13: shoot log 'X | X'; expression-4.71); (b) nothing says a chart's focus is built over that chart's `data`: n16 built it over the weigh-in days only while the chart drew every day, so a pointer on a gap day matched nothing and neither the hero nor the dim followed the pointer (expression-4.83, .92, .93); (c) `x.ticks` as a list labels exactly the bands named (`docs/cartesian-chart.md:90`), and no skill text points at it for naming the bars that matter, so n13 printed four of 18 payees and named none of the top risers (.63, .66); (d) a frame's skeleton draws what the part declares, and nothing tells a builder to keep declaring sub, rows, delta and footer in loading: n16 dropped them and its strip lost 56 px and its cards 137 px while loading (.86, .89). The rest are devices the text names and builders skipped: a when-question drawn as a table (n09 .47, .51, .60), two orders in one list (c14 .1), the answer as a faint band or a bare name with nothing on the mark (n04 .28, .33; c15 .13; n16 .79), the second card of a page without a pill or footer pairs (n13 .68, .78; n16 .94; n04 .35, .46; n09 .52, .61; c14 .6, .12), one fact stated three to five times (n13 .74; n09 .58; c15 .24; c14 .10; n04 .42; n16 .90), colour that says rise in the chart and fall in the table (n13 .64; n16 .80; n04 .31; n09 .49), a long table stacked under the chart (n13 .75; n09 .59) and an axis with no unit (c14 .3; n04 .32; n16 .81).
what: Agent text only: the linked-parts example announces once, the focus is built over the chart's data, the bars that matter are named through `x.ticks` or a text mark, every phase keeps its declarations, and the form, anatomy, word-economy and colour lines get the worked cases this cycle lost points on.
owns: packages/basalt-ui/agent/rules/basalt-charts.md and basalt-page.md (one line each at most, within the shipped-rule budget)
packages/basalt-ui/docs/** text through its generator (no generated file edited by hand)
the dogfooded copies under .claude/skills and .claude/rules (make sync-self, its own commit)

change: (1) `references/linked-parts.md`: drop the `{focus.live}` line beside a `CartesianChart` that takes `focus`; say in one sentence that the chart renders the live region and that a page renders `focus.live` itself only where no chart takes the focus (a seam-only list) (c15, n13). (2) basalt-charts: a chart's `useChartFocus` is built over the same array the chart draws (`data`); a list that shows a subset maps rows to that focus by id, never by a second focus (n16; c15 built an id map for its candidate list). (3) Answer on the mark: name the marks that matter, not all of them: on a band axis `x.ticks` as a list of the keys that matter, elsewhere an engine `text` mark placed by `chartLabels`; a band or zone that is the answer carries its words (n13, n04, c15, n16). (4) references/states.md: a part keeps every declaration (sub, rows, delta, footer) in every phase, with a placeholder value where there is none yet, because its skeleton draws what it declares; hiding a prop in loading shrinks the frame (n16; n13 passed dash placeholders by hand in round 1). (5) The form step gets two worked lines: a question of when is a time axis with the boundary drawn, never a table alone (n09); a ranking is one order that is also the mark order (c14), and a commitment is split by what makes it up (n13). (6) Card anatomy: every card of a page carries its figure's delta pill and footer pairs, not only the first; ids, repos and times in monospace (n13, n16, n04, n09, c14, c15). (7) Word economy: one more worked before and after built from this cycle's repeats, the period said once (n13, n09, c15, c14, n04, n16). (8) Colour as state across parts: a rise is one hue in the chart and the table pill; the accent marks the answer (the next run, the leader) and nothing else (n13, n16, n04, n09). (9) One view: a list longer than the chart sits beside it in its own scroll region at `@wide`, and a box holds its content's height (n13, n09, c14, n04). (10) Units: a count axis and a share-of-limit axis carry a caption, and a y format keeps a decimal for a domain under 2 units (c14, n04, n16).
